questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The book, B. which you recommended, C. was interesting and D. an easily read.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. an easily read .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"an easily read"** contains a grammatical error.
 
• The word **"read"** in this context is used as an adjective, which is incorrect. It should be replaced with **"readable"**, which is the correct adjective form.
 
• The correct phrase should be **"an easily readable"**, as it properly modifies the noun **"book"**.

Correct sentence: *The book, which you recommended, was interesting and **easily readable**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Common error when using adjectives and adverbs:**

 
 
• Adjectives modify nouns (e.g., readable book).
 
• Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs (e.g., easily readable).
 
 
 
• **Correcting misplaced modifiers:**

 
 
• Ensure modifiers are placed next to the word they describe to avoid confusion.
 
• For example: Incorrect - "She almost drove her kids to school every day." Correct - "She drove her kids to school almost every day."
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction:

He neither attended the seminar ___________submitted his report on time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. nor .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence begins with the word "**neither**," which is a correlative conjunction that works in pairs. It requires "**nor**" to complete the structure.
 
• The correct form is "**neither...nor**," which is used to connect two negative ideas in a sentence.
 
• Using "**nor**" after "neither" ensures proper grammatical structure and meaning.

Correct sentence: *He neither attended the seminar **nor** submitted his report on time*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neither...nor:** Used to connect two negative ideas.
 
 
• **Example:** She neither enjoys cooking nor cleaning.
 
• **Usage: **Indicates that both actions or ideas are not true or do not happen.
 
 
 
• **Other conjunctions:**
 
 
• **But also:** Used with "not only" to add emphasis to two ideas.
 
• **Or:** Indicates alternatives or choices.
 
• **And:** Used to connect similar ideas.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Idiosyncrasy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Peculiarity .

__
 
• The word **Idiosyncrasy** refers to a distinctive or peculiar characteristic, habit, or behavior that is unique to an individual.
 
• Among the given options:
 
 
• **Option 1: Commonalty** means shared features or common aspects, which is opposite in meaning to idiosyncrasy.
 
• **Option 2: Normality** refers to being normal or usual, which does not match the meaning of idiosyncrasy.
 
• **Option 3: Peculiarity** refers to a unique or unusual characteristic, which is a synonym of idiosyncrasy.
 
• **Option 4: Conformity** refers to compliance or aligning with standards or norms, which is opposite to idiosyncrasy.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the most appropriate synonym for **Idiosyncrasy** is **Peculiarity**.

Correct sentence: *The word "idiosyncrasy" is best represented by the synonym **peculiarity**, which captures its meaning of uniqueness or distinctiveness.*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synonyms:** Other synonyms for idiosyncrasy include "quirk," "eccentricity," and "individuality."
 
• **Antonyms:** Words like "normality," "conformity," and "commonality" are antonyms of idiosyncrasy.
</ul

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. smoke and mirrors .

• The idiom **"smoke and mirrors"** is used to describe actions or statements intended to confuse or deceive, often to mislead people into believing something that isn't true.
 
• In the given sentence, the politician’s speech is described as being full of vague promises, which means it lacks substance and is intended to create a false impression. Thus, the phrase **"smoke and mirrors"** fits perfectly.
 
• The other options do not fit the context:

• **A red herring:** Refers to a distraction or something intended to divert attention.
 
• **The last straw:** Refers to the final problem or difficulty that makes a situation unbearable.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The politician’s speech was full of vague promises but ultimately it was just **smoke and mirrors**.*

• Using idioms effectively can add depth and color to both spoken and written communication.

questions.question: What is one major benefit of increasing mental health awareness?

options.text: It makes people ashamed to talk about mental health
It encourages early intervention and better long-term outcomes
It encourages people to hide their mental health issues
It discourages people from seeking treatment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states: **"It promotes early intervention, which is necessary for better long-term outcomes and successful therapy."**
 
• The author argues that awareness helps dismantle the "historical taboo" and "de-stigmatize conditions," which directly leads to more effective, timely care.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The text says awareness helps people seek treatment **"without feeling ashamed."**
 
• **Option 3:** Increasing knowledge encourages people to **seek treatment**, not hide their issues.
 
• **Option 4:** Awareness **encourages** (rather than discourages) people to seek treatment by removing the fear of judgment.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In exams, questions often test your ability to distinguish between "consequences of stigma" and "benefits of awareness." Option 2 is a positive outcome, which aligns with the overall supportive tone of the passage.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **De-stigmatize:** To remove negative associations or social shame connected to a particular condition or behavior.
 
• **On par with:** Equal to or at the same level as something else.
 
• **Early Intervention:** Identifying and providing support for a condition at the earliest possible stage.
 
• **Coping Mechanisms:** Strategies people use to manage stress or difficult emotions.

questions.question: How does mental health awareness help reduce stigma?

options.text: By promoting a culture of silence around mental health issues
By encouraging people to feel ashamed about seeking help
By increasing knowledge and encouraging people to seek treatment
By discouraging open discussions about mental health

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states: **"Increasing knowledge helps de-stigmatize conditions... by encouraging people to seek treatment without feeling ashamed or afraid of being judged."**
 
• By replacing "historical taboo" and silence with **knowledge** and **education**, society shifts toward a culture that is "supportive and understanding."
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The text notes that "historical taboo" **silenced** discussions, whereas awareness is the solution that ends that silence.
 
• **Option 2:** Awareness allows people to seek help **"without feeling ashamed."**
 
• **Option 4:** The goal of awareness is to make mental health an "essential part of contemporary society," which requires **encouraging** rather than discouraging open discussions.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, questions about "How" usually require identifying the **mechanism** of change. In this passage, the mechanism is "Increasing knowledge," which leads to the result of "encouraging treatment."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **De-stigmatize:** To remove the negative social "mark" or shame associated with a condition.
 
• **Taboo:** A social custom forbidding or restricting a particular practice or association.
 
• **Contemporary:** Belonging to or occurring in the present.
 
• **Intervention:** Action taken to improve a medical or psychological situation.

questions.question: How does increasing public awareness of mental health conditions benefit the community?

options.text: By discouraging individuals from seeking treatment

By making it harder to find mental health services
By ignoring the symptoms and conditions of mental health

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

__
 
• The passage specifically highlights the community's role: **"increasing public awareness... gives power to the community to offer sympathy and support to individuals experiencing challenges."**
 
• It explains that this is achieved by **informing the community** about symptoms, coping mechanisms, and available services.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The text states that awareness **encourages** (not discourages) people to seek treatment by removing shame.
 
• **Option 3:** Awareness informs people about **"services available,"** making it easier, not harder, to find help.
 
• **Option 4:** The purpose of awareness is to **inform** people about symptoms, which is the opposite of ignoring them.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In competitive exams, questions about the "benefit" of a concept often focus on the **social impact** mentioned in the text. Here, the text moves from individual benefits (seeking treatment) to collective benefits (community support).*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The text explicitly states that mental health should be **"on par with bodily health,"** meaning it values both.

• **Option 4:** The passage describes mental health awareness as an **"essential part of contemporary society,"** which is the opposite of ignoring it.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Whatever floats your boat

options.text: Something that is easy to do

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. Something that makes you happy .

__
 
• The idiom "**Whatever floats your boat**" is an informal phrase used to express that someone should do what makes them happy or satisfies them, even if others might not agree or find it interesting.
 
• It emphasizes **personal choice** and **individual satisfaction**.
 
• It does not imply something impossible, easy, or universally accepted, as suggested by the other options.

Correct sentence: *If listening to classical music helps you relax, then that’s what you should do—whatever floats your boat!*.

• **Origin of the idiom:** 
 
 
• The phrase likely originated in the 20th century and draws a comparison to boats floating on water. The idea is that just as a boat floats when it’s in its natural state, people are happiest when they do what suits them best.
 
 
 
• **Similar idioms:**
 
 
• "To each their own" — Meaning everyone has their own preferences.
 
• "Different strokes for different folks" — Meaning people like different things.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

Let the documents be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.

options.text: You should submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.
The documents will be submitted to the head of the department by the end of the week.
Let the head of the department submit the documents by the end of the week.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**, where the action is emphasized rather than the doer.
 
• To convert it to the **active voice**, the subject performing the action must be made explicit.
 
• The active form of the sentence is **imperative**, as it directly instructs someone to perform an action.

Correct sentence: *Submit the documents to the head of the department by the end of the week.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active vs Passive Voice:**
 
 
• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action. Example: "She submitted the report."
 
• **Passive Voice:** The action is performed on the subject. Example: "The report was submitted by her."
 
• **Key difference:** Active voice focuses on the performer of the action, while passive voice emphasizes the action itself.
 
 
 
• **Imperative Sentences:**
 
 
• Imperatives are used to give commands, instructions, or requests.
 
• Example: "Write your name on the form."
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The librarian told the child, "You should not be making so much noise, because the other students have been trying to study for their exams."

options.text: The librarian told the child that he should not be making so much noise, because the other students had been trying to study for their exams.
The librarian told the child that he should not have been making so much noise, because the other students have been trying to study for their exams.
The librarian told the child that he would not be making so much noise, because the other students had been trying to study for their exams.
The librarian told the child that he should not be making so much noise, because the other students have been trying to study for their exams.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The librarian told the child that he should not be making so much noise, because the other students had been trying to study for their exams.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is written in **direct speech**, where the librarian is speaking directly to the child.
 
• To convert this into **indirect speech**, the pronouns, tense, and expressions need to be adjusted accordingly.
 
• Since the reporting verb is in the past tense ("told"), the verbs in the reported speech will also shift to the past tense.
 
• The present perfect tense "have been trying" changes to the past perfect tense "had been trying" in indirect speech.
 
• The modal verb "should" remains unchanged as it is used to express advice or obligation.

Correct sentence: *The librarian told the child that he should not be making so much noise, because the other students had been trying to study for their exams.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Direct Speech:** The exact words spoken by the speaker are enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The speaker's words are reported without quotation marks, and the sentence structure and tense are modified appropriately.
 
• **Rules for converting direct to indirect speech:**
 
 
• Change pronouns to match the perspective of the reporting sentence.
 
• Adjust the verb tense based on the reporting verb (past tense reporting verb requires tense changes).
 
• Modify time and place expressions if necessary (e.g., "today" changes to "that day").
 
 
</ul

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"most"** is used to form the superlative degree of adjectives, but it cannot be paired with an adjective that is already in its superlative form, such as **"toughest."**
 
• The correct form is simply **"the toughest exam"** without the word **"most."**
 
• Using **"most toughest"** is redundant and grammatically incorrect.

Correct sentence: *This is the toughest exam that I have ever taken.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Superlative Degree:**

 
 
• **Definition:** Used to compare three or more things, showing the highest degree of the quality being described.
 
• **Example:** "This is the tallest building in the city."
 
• **Rule:** Do not use "most" with adjectives that already have superlative forms ending in "-est" (e.g., tallest, smartest, toughest).
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Redundancy: Using both "most" and the "-est" form together (e.g., "most fastest").
 
• Incorrect pairing of comparative and superlative forms.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The fraud comes at a time when the unregulated finance industry is facing a crisis **on its way of **high-interest rates and low repayment of loans.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. in the way of .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence discusses the challenges faced by the unregulated finance industry due to high-interest rates and low repayment of loans.
 
• The phrase **"in the way of"** is commonly used to indicate the presence of something as a barrier, obstacle, or challenge, making it the most appropriate choice.
 
• Other options, such as "because manner of" or "by way of," do not fit the context grammatically or logically, as they change the meaning or make the sentence awkward.

Correct sentence: *The fraud comes at a time when the unregulated finance industry is facing a crisis in the way of high-interest rates and low repayment of loans*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of "in the way of":**

 
 
• This phrase is used to refer to something that acts as an obstacle or hindrance.
 
• **Example:** There is nothing in the way of achieving your dreams if you work hard.
 
 
 
• **Usage of "by way of":**
 
 
• This phrase is used to indicate a method or means of doing something.
 
• **Example:** He apologized by way of a handwritten note.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

They had not closed the shop.

options.text: The shop has not been closed by them.
The shop was not closed by them..
The shop had not been closed by them.
The shop is not closed by them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. The shop had not been closed by them .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the** past perfect tense** (had not closed).
 
• When converting a sentence from active to passive voice, the structure changes but the tense remains the same.
 
• In the past perfect tense, the passive voice structure is: **"had + not + been + past participle"**.
 
• Thus, the correct transformation of "They had not closed the shop" into passive voice is: **"The shop had not been closed by them."**

Correct sentence: *The shop had not been closed by them*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Passive Voice Basics:**
 
 
• Used when the focus is on the action or the object receiving the action, rather than the subject performing it.
 
• Structure: **Object + auxiliary verb (form of "to be") + past participle + (optional: "by + subject").**
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• Active: She writes the report. → Passive: The report is written by her.
 
• Active: They were cleaning the room. → Passive: The room was being cleaned by them.
 
• Active: He had completed the task. → Passive: The task had been completed by him.
 
 

49:T

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

He said that if he were to receive a promotion, he would buy his family a bigger house.

options.text: He said, "If I received a promotion, I would buy my family a bigger house."
He said, "If I were to receive a promotion, I would buy my family a bigger house."
He said, "If I receive a promotion, I will buy my family a bigger house."
He said, "If I had received a promotion, I would have bought my family a bigger house."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He said, "If I were to receive a promotion, I would buy my family a bigger house."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is expressed in **indirect speech**, and the task is to convert it into **direct speech.**
 
• The sentence describes a hypothetical situation using the **second conditional**, characterized by the structure ***"If + past simple, would + base verb."***
 
• In direct speech, the speaker's exact words are quoted, retaining the structure and tense of the original sentence.
 
• The correct direct speech version is: *He said, "If I were to receive a promotion, I would buy my family a bigger house."*

Correct sentence: *If I were to receive a promotion, I **would buy** my family a bigger house.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1st Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Present Simple, will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.
 
• **Usage:** Describes real or possible situations in the future with likely outcomes.
 
 
 
• **2nd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Simple, would + base verb.
 
• **Example:** If I were rich, I would travel the world.
 
• **Usage:** Describes hypothetical or unreal situations in the present or future.
 
 
 
• **3rd Conditional Sentence:**
 
 
• **Structure:** If + Past Perfect, would have + past participle.
 
• **Example:** If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
 
• **Usage:** Refers to unreal past situations and their imagined outcomes.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He started assembling the deck planks, fastening each one in a neat, even line.

Q. He made sure that every angle was precisely square when he constructed the deck with beams and joists.

R. He prepared the foundation by excavating holes and positioning the building's columns.

S. He took a step back and admired the new outdoor area, a sturdy deck that was made to stay.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. R, Q, P, S .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sequence of events in the paragraph describes the process of constructing a deck step by step, starting with the foundation and ending with admiration of the final product.
 
• The correct sequence is as follows:
 
 
• **R:** Preparing the foundation by excavating holes and positioning the building's columns.
 
• **Q:** Constructing the deck with beams and joists, ensuring precise angles.
 
• **P:** Assembling the deck planks in a neat, even line.
 
• **S:** Admiring the completed sturdy deck.
 
 
 
• This logical order ensures that the steps are described in a meaningful and grammatically correct manner.

Correct sentence sequence: *R, Q, P, S*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When solving such rearrangement questions:
 
 
• Identify the logical sequence of events or ideas.
 
• Look for connecting words, phrases, or steps to help determine the proper order.
 
• Ensure that the paragraph flows naturally and grammatically correct.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. The method, which is titled the Socratic method, is a cornerstone of Western philosophy.

Q. Socrates believed that the path to knowledge was not through lecturing but through a systematic process of questioning.

R. He would probe his students mercilessly, taking them through a chain of logical conclusions.

S. Its goal was not to provide answers but to force the individual to discover the truth for themselves.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Q, P, R, S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph revolves around explaining the Socratic method, a systematic process of questioning for discovering truth.
 
• Statement Q introduces the belief of Socrates, which forms the foundation of the Socratic method.
 
• Statement P names the method and highlights its importance in Western philosophy.
 
• Statement R describes how Socrates conducted his questioning process with his students.
 
• Statement S concludes by explaining the ultimate goal of the method.

Correct sequence: *Q, P, R, S*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Logical Flow:** The paragraph must begin with the introduction of Socrates' belief (Q), followed by identifying the method (P), describing the process (R), and concluding with its purpose (S).
 
• **Elimination of Options:**
 
 
• Option 2 (S, P, R, Q) disrupts the logical order by starting with the conclusion.
 
• Option 3 (Q, R, S, P) misplaces the naming of the method after the description of its process.
 
• Option 4 (S, Q, R, P) incorrectly begins with the conclusion and places the introduction later.
 
 
</ul
